VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The endpoint \(x=1\) is correctly excluded from the interior, so the derivative-bound condition of the corollary is required only on \((1,\infty)\) where it holds with the constant \(1/\iota(2)\). Continuity at the endpoint is obtained from differentiability on the larger domain \((0,\infty)\) and the restriction clause, satisfying the corollary’s continuity hypothesis. The interval \([1,\infty)\) is order-convex and nondegenerate. No counterexample exists; the inequality is the standard bound \(|\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y}|\le \frac12|x-y|\) for \(x,y\ge1\), which is tight at the endpoint.
